items.title: Is Consciousness More Fundamental Than God? | Swami Sarvapriyananda
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if God, consciousness, the universe, and you are all manifestations of one deeper reality?*

Swami Sarvapriyananda explains the Advaita Vedanta conception of Brahman as limitless existence, consciousness, and bliss, and explores why even the personal God of religion is ultimately grounded in this more fundamental reality.

0:00 What Is Ultimate Reality in Hindu Philosophy?
1:11 Brahman Is Existence, Consciousness, and Bliss
3:12 Existence Is More Fundamental Than Existing Things
4:37 You Are That: The Central Teaching of Advaita
5:20 Are You the Body, Mind, or Consciousness?
7:08 What Is the Relationship Between Brahman and God?
9:36 Is God Less Fundamental Than Brahman?

*Swami Sarvapriyananda* is a Hindu monk of the Ramakrishna Order and head of the Vedanta Society of New York. He is a prominent teacher of Vedanta and has spoken internationally on Hindu philosophy, spirituality, and interfaith dialogue.

items.title: Did Morality Evolve Through Group Competition? | Rachell Powell
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if some of the best clues to the evolution of human morality come from ants and bees?*

Rachell Powell explores why inclusive fitness may not fully explain biological altruism and argues that group competition and social organization could help explain the emergence of ultra-cooperation, social norms, and morality-like systems in both humans and social insects.

0:00 Why Is Altruism an Evolutionary Puzzle?
1:20 Moving Beyond Inclusive Fitness
2:17 Did Morality Evolve Through Group Competition?
3:02 Is Morality Unique to Humans?
4:08 Humans and Social Insects Share Ultra-Cooperation
5:16 Can Insect Societies Illuminate Human Morality?
7:37 Social Norms as Functional Structures

Philosopher *Rachell Powell* explores how modern healthcare reshapes human evolution. By relaxing natural selection, medicine may be pushing humanity toward greater dependence on advanced technology—raising a striking paradox: to preserve human health as we know it, we may need to intervene more, not less.

items.title: Should We Choose a Theory of Consciousness? | Alex Gómez-Marín
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if every major theory of consciousness is partly right and partly wrong?*

Alex Gómez-Marín explains why he resists committing to materialism, dualism, idealism, or even panpsychism, arguing for intellectual flexibility while asking whether truth alone should guide our theories or whether goodness and beauty also reveal something about reality.

0:00 Why Stay Agnostic About Consciousness?
0:36 What Is Your Best Theory of Consciousness?
1:02 Are All Theories Partly Right and Partly Wrong?
2:07 Why Committing to One Theory Can Be Dangerous
2:49 Does Experience Transcend Theory?
4:30 Should Ethics Influence Theories of Reality?
6:08 Do Truth, Goodness, and Beauty Reveal Reality?

*Alex Gómez-Marín* is a Spanish physicist turned neuroscientist. He holds a PhD in theoretical physics and a Masters in biophysics from the University of Barcelona. He was a research fellow at the EMBL-CRG Centre for Genomic Regulation and at the Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown in Lisbon. His research spans from the origins of the arrow of time in inert systems, to the neurobiology of action-perception in living organisms such as flies, worms, mice, and humans.

items.title: DNA Is Not a Program for Building an Organism | Paul Griffiths
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Is an organism really programmed into its DNA like software into a computer?*

Paul Griffiths argues that the genetic code has genuine scientific meaning, but it cannot contain instructions for building an entire organism. Development instead depends on a layered system of interactions extending beyond DNA to molecules, cells, and their environments.

0:00 Information Is Biology's Latest Metaphor
1:22 Evolution Does Not Write an Organism Into DNA
2:25 DNA Depends on Its Cellular Environment
3:07 The Genetic Code Cannot Tell You to Grow a Leg
4:52 Genetic Code and Genetic Programs Are Different
6:19 Development Requires Layers of Control
7:41 Information Theory Can Model Biological Causation

*Paul Griffiths* is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney and works primarily in the Philosophy of Science and more particularly Philosophy of Biology.

items.title: The Limits of Theodicies for the Problem of Evil | Michael Tooley
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Can any theodicy explain the enormity of evil?*

Michael Tooley tests free will, soul-making, natural law, karma, reincarnation, and the afterlife, asking whether these responses can account for horrendous suffering without requiring a radically different kind of world.

0:00 Theodicies Confront the Problem of Evil
1:10 Free Will Faces Scientific and Philosophical Challenges

*Michael Tooley* is Emeritus Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder. He received a Boulder Faculty Assembly Excellence in Research Award in 1998 for his book _Time, Tense, and Causation,_ and is the author of the new book _Causation: A Defense of a Non-Reductionist Approach_ (Oxford, 2026).

<article>*Should a theory of consciousness be judged only by whether it is true, or also by what it allows us to understand and do?*

Jeffrey Mishlove argues that metaphysical theories may resist ordinary tests of truth, making their pragmatic value important as well. Yet when comparing the major alternatives, he leans toward idealism and an expansive view of the collective unconscious.

items.title: Why It Matters Which Species Go Extinct | Derek Turner
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Can fossils help us make better decisions about today's biodiversity crisis?*

Derek Turner says paleontology cannot derive ethical principles from the fossil record, but extinction selectivity may reveal something crucial that extinction rates alone miss: which species are most vulnerable and why.

0:00 Paleontology and the Biodiversity Crisis
2:00 More Than Rates and Magnitudes
3:47 The Ethics of De-Extinction

*Derek Turner* is the Class of '43 Professor of Philosophy and Director of the Goodwin-Niering Center for the Environment at Connecticut College. A recipient of both the John S. King Teaching Award and the Nisbet Rash Research Award, his work focuses on the philosophy of paleontology, macroevolution, and deep time. He is the author of _Paleontology: A Philosophical Introduction_ and _Paleoaesthetics and the Practice of Paleontology,_ as well as a co-founder of the philosophy of paleontology blog _Extinct._
